what: LM-ATTN (2026-10-18): the 1,000-step language-model run at four threads under the attention bit (ATTN-FMA) -- LM-PAIRED's five seeds (20261011, 1001, 2002, 3003, 4004), five arms a seed in one session, their order rotated seed by seed: BCIR under bf16+exp+reduce+attn and bf16+exp+reduce, under kblock+exp+reduce+attn and kblock+exp+reduce (FP32 GEMMs), and torch.compile with fused AdamW under torch.autocast(cpu, bfloat16) (LM-BF16's faster PyTorch bf16 arm). The analysis was fixed before the runs (paired_attn.py's docstring): per pair of arms the ratio of the median warm steps per seed, their geometric mean and a 95% Student-t interval on the log ratios, and a +-0.01-nat margin on the test cross-entropy difference for every pair; and whether the arms without the bit end in LM-BF16's states.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207: AMX-BF16 and AVX512-BF16; the instance of ../ and ../../../2026-10-17/bf16/lm/), GCC 13.3 (the trainer builds), PyTorch 2.13.0 at four intra-op threads, Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); every record names commit b73206e (runtime/c identical to it); indicative wall times, no PMU
reading: Median warm step, BCIR bf16+attn / PyTorch bf16 / BCIR bf16 / BCIR FP32+attn / BCIR FP32: seed 1001 68.5 / 131.2 / 71.8 / 165.3 / 170.3 ms; seed 2002 70.8 / 147.3 / 72.7 / 165.7 / 170.6 ms; seed 3003 68.3 / 142.9 / 72.0 / 163.6 / 169.2 ms; seed 4004 69.7 / 138.9 / 68.2 / 162.2 / 169.7 ms; seed 20261011 77.8 / 155.3 / 82.0 / 177.6 / 175.7 ms. The bcir-bf16 and bcir arms end in LM-BF16's states on 5 of 5 seeds each (states_as_lm_bf16): the contracts without the attention bit are unchanged over 1,000 steps. Peak RSS 540 MB for BCIR's bf16 arms and 529-530 for its FP32 arms against 1,132-1,148 for PyTorch's; the persistent state the same 157,390,848 bytes on every arm.
